items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: I played with Dexter Gordon, Johnny Griffin, Benny Bailey

ctx.x: Wow. And playing mostly with European musicians? © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Sometimes with American musicians, sometime with European musicians. I played with Dexter Gordon, Johnny Griffin, Benny Bailey, oh just a host of guys that were living — Kenny Clarke. All the guys that were living over there and also with the European musicians. We made radio shows. Because see in every city in Europe there’s a radio band that is subsidized by the government to play a certain amount of jazz every year.

items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That band, Joe Haider, we were co-leaders... Johnny Griffin... Dexter was in that band, and Benny Bailey was in that band, Johnny Griffin... I got Dexter, Johnny Griffin, Benny Bailey, Art Farmer. The whole band was like that... I wrote the music for the band.

ctx.x: Who was the “we”? What circle did you walk into, of musicians?

With Dexter and the guys. Don Byas, Dexter, Art Farmer, Benny Bailey, Johnny Griffin, Kenny Clarke. I worked a lot with Kenny. They treated Kenny so good that Kenny wouldn’t – if you said anything about France, Kenny would really jump on you, because he lived in France for a long time, and without a green card. So he didn’t have to pay taxes. When it came time for him to get his green card, all the money that he owed, the government wiped the slate clean, and gave him his green card. They loved him so much there.
Was that the only European circle? Was that your primary European circle? Was there – did you – were there people in Germany and Sweden and another group in Denmark?
